title: Volatility is the asset you trade with options
summary: When you trade options you are really trading volatility. Buy cheap volatility and sell expensive volatility. IV percentile only shows where implied volatility sits versus the last 12 months. Comparing implied volatility with realized volatility shows whether volatility is actually rich or cheap. The speaker calls his version of this metric VAY and is building a browser extension for it.

steps.caption: Implied volatility: what the market pays you today for taking volatility risk.
Realized volatility: how much the stock actually moved in the recent past.
IV above RV means volatility is rich: sell. IV below RV means it is cheap: buy.
IV percentile only ranks the IV level over 12 months. It does not say whether IV is rich versus what the stock delivers.

takeaways: Options trade volatility; buy it cheap and sell it rich.
IV percentile shows the level of implied volatility, not its value.
Compare implied with realized volatility to judge rich or cheap.
caveats: VAY (Volatility Adjusted Yield) is the speaker's own proprietary metric. Its formula is not given and its results are unverified.
The free Chrome extension and its release date are promotional claims, not verified.
